issues.legal_issue: The restriction against an even-numbered arbitral tribunal is derogable, and a party that does not timely object to the tribunal’s composition waives the objection.
material_facts: The parties agreed to have two persons resolve their dispute, and all parties participated in the proceedings before them.
The tribunal issued an award, after which two parties sought to set it aside on the ground that the tribunal had an even number of arbitrators.
Those parties had not objected to the tribunal’s composition before the tribunal as required during the arbitration.
issues.conclusion: The restriction in Section 10 is derogable when read with Sections 4 and 16. A party may object to the tribunal’s composition, but must do so no later than the submission of its statement of defence; a party that does not timely object is deemed to have waived the objection. An agreement to arbitrate before two persons is not invalid merely because it provides for an even number.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 10 and 16 must be read together: an objection to the composition of the tribunal may be raised before the tribunal under Section 16(2), even by a party that participated in appointing an arbitrator, and failure to raise it within the prescribed time results in waiver under Section 4. Section 16 permits the tribunal to rule on objections going to the root of its jurisdiction, as held in Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. v. Rani Construction Pvt. Ltd. Section 11(3) provides for a third, presiding arbitrator in a three-arbitrator proceeding; the Court stated that two arbitrators may appoint a third if they differ. The Act’s limits on judicial intervention and on setting aside awards also support treating the composition objection as waivable.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge and agreed_even_number_tribunal and knew_composition_objection and participated_without_objecting and no_timely_tribunal_objection

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party seeks to set aside an award made in an arbitration.
predicates.agreed_even_number_tribunal: The parties agreed to an arbitral tribunal with an even number of members.
predicates.knew_composition_objection: The party knew the facts giving rise to its objection to the tribunal’s composition.
predicates.participated_without_objecting: The party participated in the arbitration without objecting to the tribunal’s composition.
predicates.no_timely_tribunal_objection: The party did not raise the composition objection before the tribunal within the time allowed for doing so.

issues.definition: When a party that knows the basis for a composition objection participates in an arbitration under an agreed even-numbered tribunal and does not timely raise the objection, the objection is treated as waived in a challenge to the resulting award.

issues.legal_issue: An award cannot be challenged on the ground that the tribunal’s composition conflicts with the governing arbitration law when that composition accords with the parties’ agreement.
material_facts: The parties agreed to have two persons resolve their dispute, and the tribunal’s composition followed that agreement.
The award was challenged on the ground that an even-numbered tribunal conflicted with the governing arbitration law.
issues.conclusion: Section 34(2)(a)(v) does not permit a challenge based merely on a conflict with the Act where the tribunal’s composition is in accordance with the parties’ agreement. The statutory exception concerning non-derogable provisions applies when the composition or procedure is not in accordance with the agreement; the provision also addresses cases where there is no agreement and the composition or procedure does not conform to Part I.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 34(2)(a)(v), the opening condition is that the tribunal’s composition or procedure was not in accordance with the parties’ agreement. The exception for an agreement conflicting with a non-derogable provision, and the alternative where there is no agreement, operate only after that condition is met. Sections 5 and 34 reflect the Act’s limited approach to judicial intervention and award challenges.

predicates.award_set_aside_application: A party applies to a court to set aside an arbitral award.
predicates.composition_conforms_to_party_agreement: The composition of the arbitral tribunal accords with the parties’ agreement.
predicates.challenge_based_only_on_statutory_compos: The party relies on the claim that the agreed composition conflicts with a statutory requirement.

issues.definition: In an application to set aside an award, a statutory-composition-conflict claim does not provide a ground for challenge when the tribunal’s composition accords with the parties’ agreement.
